public_packet.policy: Apply these rules in order; the first one that matches decides the alert. (1) MERGE: only alerts whose source is "monitor" can be duplicates or roots; synthetic alerts are never merged (rule 2 closes them). A monitor alert is a duplicate if another monitor alert with the same service_id and the same signature was opened earlier: merge it into the earliest one (the root; give its id as `into`). If two alerts opened in the same minute, the one with the lower id counts as earlier. Merge duplicates even if the root itself gets closed. The root is never merged. (2) CLOSE: if the alert's source is "synthetic" (test probes), or its service is in maintenance and the alert's severity is not "critical". (3) ESCALATE (page the on-call): if severity is "critical"; or "high" and it has been open more than 30 minutes; or "medium" and open more than 120 minutes (counting from now). "low" never escalates.
